description: We are passionate about space exploration, data analysis, and using technology to solve real-world problems. We love tackling creative challenges and building impactful solutions using open-source data.
summary: Zénith Earth turns 20 years of NASA satellite data into simple local climate reports. Just click any city on our map. The app fetches NASA surface temperature data (MOD11A2) and filters out normal seasonal swings. It calculates real long-term warming, projects future heat trends, and compares Urban vs. Rural areas. Anyone can now spot dangerous urban heat islands early and plan cooler cities—no complex scientific software needed.
details:
Zénith Earth turns over 20 years of NASA satellite temperature data into simple local climate reports. Users pick any location on a world map. The platform fetches NASA MODIS Land Surface Temperature data (MOD11A2), removes seasonal weather cycles with STL decomposition, and measures long-term warming using the Mann-Kendall test and Sen’s slope. It also projects future warming with linear regression and compares Urban vs. Rural heat levels.

Benefits & Intended Impact Raw satellite files are hard to use without specialized software. Zénith Earth makes this data accessible to everyone in one click. Tested on Ben Guerir, Phoenix, São Paulo, and Yaoundé, it helps urban planners, researchers, and citizens detect heat islands early and build cooler, more resilient cities.

Tools & Technologies

  • NASA Data: NASA Earthdata & AppEEARS API (MODIS MOD11A2 Land Surface Temperature).
  • Backend & Math: Python, FastAPI, pandas, scipy, statsmodels (hosted on Render).
  • Frontend: React, Vite, Leaflet maps (hosted on Vercel).

Creativity & Key Factors Instead of showing confusing raw graphs, we turn complex math into clear warming verdicts and simple Urban vs. Rural comparisons. Our team also built a fast cache and a smart backup model. This ensures the app responds instantly, even when NASA servers are slow.
